To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
marked elevation of SGOT or SGPT is due to acute inflammatory liver cell damage caused by impacted or migrating bile duct stones, which is reversible and transient.

the main liver histology in acute gallstone disease is necrosis of liver cell, and the marked elevation of serum SGOT or SGPT in acute gallstone patients is due to an acute liver cell injury caused either by impacted or floating stones in the bile duct.

the marked elevation of serum SGOT/SGPT in patients with acute cholecystitis or acute cholangitis is transient and reversible and is due to an acute liver cell injury caused mainly by impacted or migrating stones in the common bile duct.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the etiology and pathogenesis of marked elevation of serum SGOT or SGPT in patients with acute cholecystitis.
the etiology and pathogenesis of marked elevation of serum SGOT and SGPT in patients with acute biliary tract obstruction.

a study of the etiology and pathogenesis of marked elevation of serum SGOT and SGPT in patients with acute cholelithiasis, with a view to providing a rational basis for the treatment of this condition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
marked elevation of transaminase is not necessarily a poor prognostic sign in acute gallstone disease.
marked elevation of transaminase in acute gallstone disease is caused by a transient liver cell injury and not by an acute cholangitis.
in patients with acute cholecystitis and elevated serum transaminase, early surgical intervention is mandatory to prevent further damage to the liver.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the etiology and pathogenesis of marked elevation of serum liver enzymes in patients with acute cholecystitis is due to the migration of stones through the common bile duct, which causes an acute liver injury and that this injury is self-limited and reversible.
in acute gallstone disease, marked elevation of serum SGOT or SGPT might be due to acute inflammatory liver cell injuries, caused by impacted or migrating bile duct stones.
marked elevation of transaminase in acute gallstone disease is due to an acute liver cell injury, but the pathogenesis of this liver cell damage is not clear.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of elevated serum transaminases in the setting of acute gallstone disease is not necessarily indicative of a severe liver injury.

in patients with acute cholecystitis, a marked elevation of serum aminotransferase levels is not a reliable indicator of liver damage and that a high serum level of aminotransaminase does not necessarily indicate liver cell necrosis.
the presence of a stone in the common bile duct (CBD), even if it’s asymptomatic, is associated with a high risk of developing gallbladder cancer.
